---- MODULE W4Od3m0p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS a1, a2
Accts == {a1, a2}
Txns == {"t1", "t2", "t3"}
Src == [t1 |-> a1, t2 |-> a1, t3 |-> a2]
Dst == [t1 |-> a2, t2 |-> a2, t3 |-> a1]
Amt == [t1 |-> 1, t2 |-> 1, t3 |-> 1]
MaxRetry == 2
TOTAL == 3

VARIABLES bal, ver, st, snap, retries
vars == <<bal, ver, st, snap, retries>>

Init ==
  /\ bal = [x \in Accts |-> IF x = a1 THEN 2 ELSE 1]
  /\ ver = [x \in Accts |-> 0]
  /\ st = [t \in Txns |-> "pending"]
  /\ snap = [t \in Txns |-> 0]
  /\ retries = [t \in Txns |-> 0]

Begin(t) ==
  /\ st[t] = "pending"
  /\ bal[Src[t]] >= Amt[t]
  /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![Src[t]] = @ - Amt[t]]
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![t] = ver[Src[t]]]
  /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![t] = "held"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, retries>>

Commit(t) ==
  /\ st[t] = "held"
  /\ ver[Src[t]] = snap[t]
  /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![Dst[t]] = @ + Amt[t]]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![Src[t]] = @ + 1]
  /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![t] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, retries>>

Retry(t) ==
  /\ st[t] = "held"
  /\ ver[Src[t]] # snap[t]
  /\ retries[t] < MaxRetry
  /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![Src[t]] = @ + Amt[t]]
  /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![t] = "pending"]
  /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, snap>>

GiveUp(t) ==
  /\ st[t] = "held"
  /\ ver[Src[t]] # snap[t]
  /\ retries[t] >= MaxRetry
  /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![Src[t]] = @ + Amt[t]]
  /\ st' = [st EXCEPT ![t] = "void"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, snap, retries>>

Done == (\A t \in Txns : st[t] \in {"done", "void"}) /\ UNCHANGED vars
Next == (\E t \in Txns : Begin(t) \/ Commit(t) \/ Retry(t) \/ GiveUp(t)) \/ Done
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Held(t) == IF st[t] = "held" THEN Amt[t] ELSE 0
MoneyConserved ==
  (bal[a1] + bal[a2]) + (Held("t1") + Held("t2") + Held("t3")) = TOTAL
====

CONSTANTS a1 = a1  a2 = a2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MoneyConserved
nl:
An interbank settlement batch moves money between a small set of ledger accounts. Each pending transfer names a source account, a destination account, and a fixed amount. A worker begins a transfer only when the source has enough funds: it debits the source, snapshots the source account's version number, and marks the transfer as held in escrow. To finalize, the worker commits only if the source version still matches the snapshot it took, meaning no other transfer altered that account in the meantime; committing credits the destination and bumps the source version. If instead the version has changed, the optimistic attempt lost the race, so the worker returns the escrowed funds to the source and retries, up to a bounded number of attempts, after which it gives up and voids the transfer. Because the network delivers requests in any order, begins, commits, and retries for different transfers may interleave arbitrarily. No matter how they interleave, money is neither created nor destroyed: escrowed funds are always accounted for.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the sum of all account balances plus all funds currently held in escrow always equals the fixed total that existed at the start.

---- MODULE W4Od7m7p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS c1, c2, x1, x2
Cranes == {c1, c2}
Containers == {x1, x2}
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES owner, lifts, cstate, job, lifter
vars == <<owner, lifts, cstate, job, lifter>>

Init ==
  /\ owner = [c \in Containers |-> NONE]
  /\ lifts = [c \in Containers |-> 0]
  /\ cstate = [k \in Cranes |-> "free"]
  /\ job = [k \in Cranes |-> NONE]
  /\ lifter = [c \in Containers |-> NONE]

Claim(k, c) ==
  /\ cstate[k] = "free"
  /\ owner[c] = NONE
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = k]
  /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![k] = "busy"]
  /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![k] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lifts, lifter>>

Lift(k) ==
  /\ cstate[k] = "busy"
  /\ LET c == job[k] IN
       /\ lifts[c] = 0
       /\ lifts' = [lifts EXCEPT ![c] = 1]
       /\ lifter' = [lifter EXCEPT ![c] = k]
  /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![k] = "free"]
  /\ job' = [job EXCEPT ![k] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED owner

Crash(k) ==
  /\ cstate[k] # "crashed"
  /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![k] = "crashed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, lifts, job, lifter>>

Done == (\A k \in Cranes : cstate[k] \in {"free", "crashed"})
        /\ (\A c \in Containers : lifts[c] = 1 \/ owner[c] # NONE => TRUE)
        /\ (\A k \in Cranes : cstate[k] # "busy")
        /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == (\E k \in Cranes : Crash(k) \/ Lift(k) \/ (\E c \in Containers : Claim(k, c))) \/ Done
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleLift ==
  \A c \in Containers :
    /\ lifts[c] <= 1
    /\ (lifter[c] = NONE <=> lifts[c] = 0)
    /\ (lifts[c] = 1 => owner[c] = lifter[c])
====

CONSTANTS c1 = c1  c2 = c2  x1 = x1  x2 = x2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleLift
nl:
A container-ship crane yard has several cranes competing to lift a set of containers off the deck. Each container has a single ownership register that starts empty. A free crane claims a container with a compare-and-swap: it succeeds only if the register was empty, in which case the register atomically records that crane as owner and the crane becomes busy on that container. Lifting a container off the deck is irreversible and physically destructive to repeat, so a busy crane lifts its claimed container exactly once, recording itself as the lifter and returning to free while the register stays owned. A crane may crash silently at any moment; if it was holding a claim it never releases, but that only strands the container, it never causes a second lift. Because ownership is won by compare-and-swap and lifting requires holding the claim, no container is ever lifted by two cranes or lifted twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every container is lifted at most once, and a container records a lifter exactly when its lift has occurred.

---- MODULE W4Od6m4p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
CONSTANTS i1, i2, j1, j2, j3
Ctrls == {i1, i2}
Jobs == {j1, j2, j3}
Cap == 2
FREE == "free"
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES backlog, queue, log, lock, snap, cur
vars == <<backlog, queue, log, lock, snap, cur>>

InQueue(j) == \E k \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[k] = j

Init ==
  /\ backlog = Jobs
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ log = {}
  /\ lock = FREE
  /\ snap = [i \in Ctrls |-> {}]
  /\ cur = [i \in Ctrls |-> NONE]

Enqueue(j) ==
  /\ j \in backlog
  /\ Len(queue) < Cap
  /\ backlog' = backlog \ {j}
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, j)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<log, lock, snap, cur>>

Acquire(i) ==
  /\ lock = FREE
  /\ cur[i] = NONE
  /\ Len(queue) > 0
  /\ lock' = i
  /\ cur' = [cur EXCEPT ![i] = Head(queue)]
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = log]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, log>>

Commit(i) ==
  /\ lock = i
  /\ cur[i] # NONE
  /\ log' = snap[i] \cup {cur[i]}
  /\ lock' = FREE
  /\ cur' = [cur EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, queue, snap>>

Abort(i) ==
  /\ lock = i
  /\ cur[i] # NONE
  /\ backlog' = backlog \cup {cur[i]}
  /\ lock' = FREE
  /\ cur' = [cur EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, log, snap>>

Done == (backlog = {}) /\ (Len(queue) = 0) /\ (\A i \in Ctrls : cur[i] = NONE)
        /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == (\E j \in Jobs : Enqueue(j))
        \/ (\E i \in Ctrls : Acquire(i) \/ Commit(i) \/ Abort(i))
        \/ Done
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
  \A j \in Jobs :
    (j \notin backlog /\ ~InQueue(j) /\ (\A i \in Ctrls : cur[i] # j)) => j \in log
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS i1 = i1  i2 = i2  j1 = j1  j2 = j2  j3 = j3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
Two independent elevator controllers share one pool of hall-call requests in a skyscraper. New calls sit in a backlog and are admitted into a bounded dispatch queue only while the queue has room; when the queue is full, admission is refused, which is the backpressure that keeps the queue bounded. To serve a call a controller must first take the single dispatch lock: it removes the head call from the queue, records which call it is working on, and snapshots the shared served-record at that moment. It then commits by writing back the snapshot extended with the call it just handled and releasing the lock, so the shared record accumulates every served call. Because only one controller may hold the lock at a time, the read-modify-write of the shared record is serialized and no controller ever overwrites another's contribution. A controller may also abort mid-flight, returning its call to the backlog. Any call that has left the pipeline entirely must therefore be reflected in the shared record.
SAFETY PROPERTY: any call that is no longer in the backlog, the queue, or in flight at some controller has been recorded in the shared served-record, so no served call's update is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od19m5p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS r1, r2, r3, p1, p2, s1, s2
Replicas == {r1, r2, r3}
Patrons == {p1, p2}
Slots == {s1, s2}
Quorum == 2
NONE == "none"

VARIABLES vote, granted, up, want
vars == <<vote, granted, up, want>>

VotesFor(s, p) == {r \in Replicas : vote[s][r] = p}
SlotGranted(s) == \E p \in Patrons : <<s, p>> \in granted

Init ==
  /\ vote = [s \in Slots |-> [r \in Replicas |-> NONE]]
  /\ granted = {}
  /\ up = [r \in Replicas |-> TRUE]
  /\ want = [p \in Patrons |-> Slots]

CastVote(r, s, p) ==
  /\ up[r]
  /\ vote[s][r] = NONE
  /\ s \in want[p]
  /\ ~SlotGranted(s)
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![s][r] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<granted, up, want>>

Grant(s, p) ==
  /\ s \in want[p]
  /\ ~SlotGranted(s)
  /\ Cardinality(VotesFor(s, p)) >= Quorum
  /\ granted' = granted \cup {<<s, p>>}
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![p] = @ \ {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, up>>

Crash(r) ==
  /\ up[r]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, granted, want>>

Release(s, p) ==
  /\ <<s, p>> \in granted
  /\ granted' = granted \ {<<s, p>>}
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![s] = [r \in Replicas |-> NONE]]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED up

Recover(r) ==
  /\ ~up[r]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, granted, want>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Replicas, s \in Slots, p \in Patrons : CastVote(r, s, p)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, p \in Patrons : Grant(s, p) \/ Release(s, p)
  \/ \E r \in Replicas : Crash(r) \/ Recover(r)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

QuorumBacked ==
  \A s \in Slots, p \in Patrons :
    (<<s, p>> \in granted) => Cardinality(VotesFor(s, p)) >= Quorum
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS r1=r1 r2=r2 r3=r3 p1=p1 p2=p2 s1=s1 s2=s2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT QuorumBacked
nl:
A library book-reservation system runs several replica servers that must agree before a copy of a title is handed to a patron. Each copy is a slot, and each replica can cast at most one vote per slot. A patron who wants a slot has its request voted on: a live replica casts its single vote for that patron on that slot, but only while the slot is not already granted. Once a patron has collected votes from a majority quorum of replicas for a slot, the reservation is granted. Because any two majority quorums of replicas overlap in at least one replica, and no replica ever votes for two different patrons on the same slot, two patrons can never both amass a quorum for one copy. A replica may crash silently and stop voting; the votes it already cast still count, and the quorum requirement tolerates the loss. A granted reservation may later be released, which clears the votes so the copy can circulate again.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every granted reservation is backed by a majority quorum of replica votes for that patron on that copy, which since replicas never double-vote guarantees no copy is granted to two patrons at once.

---- MODULE W4Od9m2p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS co1, co2, za, zb
Coords == {co1, co2}
Zones == {za, zb}
TOTAL == 2

VARIABLES load, resv, shed, phase, vote
vars == <<load, resv, shed, phase, vote>>

Init ==
  /\ load = [z \in Zones |-> 1]
  /\ resv = [c \in Coords |-> [z \in Zones |-> 0]]
  /\ shed = 0
  /\ phase = [c \in Coords |-> "idle"]
  /\ vote = [c \in Coords |-> [z \in Zones |-> "none"]]

Begin(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "idle"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "voting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, resv, shed, vote>>

Prepare(c, z) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "voting"
  /\ vote[c][z] = "none"
  /\ load[z] >= 1
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![z] = @ - 1]
  /\ resv' = [resv EXCEPT ![c][z] = 1]
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![c][z] = "yes"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shed, phase>>

Commit(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "voting"
  /\ \A z \in Zones : vote[c][z] = "yes"
  /\ shed' = shed + resv[c][za] + resv[c][zb]
  /\ resv' = [resv EXCEPT ![c] = [z \in Zones |-> 0]]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, vote>>

Abort(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] = "voting"
  /\ \E z \in Zones : vote[c][z] = "none" /\ load[z] = 0
  /\ load' = [z \in Zones |-> load[z] + resv[c][z]]
  /\ resv' = [resv EXCEPT ![c] = [z \in Zones |-> 0]]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "aborted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shed, vote>>

Reset(c) ==
  /\ phase[c] \in {"committed", "aborted"}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![c] = [z \in Zones |-> "none"]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, resv, shed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Coords : Begin(c) \/ Commit(c) \/ Abort(c) \/ Reset(c)
  \/ \E c \in Coords, z \in Zones : Prepare(c, z)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TotalReserved == resv[co1][za] + resv[co1][zb] + resv[co2][za] + resv[co2][zb]
PowerConserved == (load[za] + load[zb]) + TotalReserved + shed = TOTAL

CONSTANTS co1=co1 co2=co2 za=za zb=zb
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PowerConserved
nl:
A power-grid load shedder uses two independent coordinators that share one pool of load zones. Shedding load is a two-phase commit across the participating zones: a coordinator first begins a transaction, then in the voting phase asks each zone to prepare by reserving one unit of its available load, which succeeds only if that zone still has a unit free. Because both coordinators draw from the same zones, they contend: a unit reserved by one coordinator is unavailable to the other, which may then be forced to abort. A coordinator commits only when every zone has voted yes, at which point all its reserved units are moved into the shed pool. If it cannot gather all votes it aborts, returning every unit it had reserved back to the zones. After committing or aborting, a coordinator resets to idle and may run again. Throughout, load is only ever moved between the zones, the coordinators' in-flight reservations, and the shed pool; it is never created or lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total available load across all zones, plus all units currently reserved in flight by either coordinator, plus the load already shed, always equals the fixed total load present at the start.

EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS f1, f2
Floors == {f1, f2}
TOTAL == 2

VARIABLES waiting, car, resv, ph, ready
vars == <<waiting, car, resv, ph, ready>>

Init ==
  /\ waiting = [f \in Floors |-> 1]
  /\ car = 0
  /\ resv = [f \in Floors |-> 0]
  /\ ph = "idle"
  /\ ready = [f \in Floors |-> FALSE]

Begin ==
  /\ ph = "idle"
  /\ ph' = "voting"
  /\ ready' = [f \in Floors |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, car, resv>>

Prepare(f) ==
  /\ ph = "voting"
  /\ ~ready[f]
  /\ waiting[f] >= 1
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
  /\ resv' = [resv EXCEPT ![f] = 1]
  /\ ready' = [ready EXCEPT ![f] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<car, ph>>

PrepareEmpty(f) ==
  /\ ph = "voting"
  /\ ~ready[f]
  /\ waiting[f] = 0
  /\ ready' = [ready EXCEPT ![f] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, car, resv, ph>>

Commit ==
  /\ ph = "voting"
  /\ \A f \in Floors : ready[f]
  /\ car' = car + resv[f1] + resv[f2]
  /\ resv' = [f \in Floors |-> 0]
  /\ ph' = "committed"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, ready>>

Reset ==
  /\ ph = "committed"
  /\ ph' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, car, resv, ready>>

  \/ Begin \/ Commit \/ Reset
  \/ \E f \in Floors : Prepare(f) \/ PrepareEmpty(f)

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PassengersConserved
nl:
An elevator bank dispatches passengers from several floors into one car using a two-phase commit so that a boarding round is atomic across all participating floors. A round begins when the coordinator moves from idle to the voting phase and clears each floor's readiness flag. During voting, each floor prepares: a floor with a waiting passenger reserves exactly one passenger to board, moving that passenger out of its waiting group and into an in-flight reservation, then marks itself ready; a floor with nobody waiting simply marks itself ready with an empty reservation. Floors may be slow to respond and prepare in any order, but none ever fails or refuses, so the coordinator always eventually sees every floor ready. Only when all floors are ready does the coordinator commit, sweeping every reserved passenger into the car and returning to a committed state. It then resets to idle and can run another round. Passengers are never created or destroyed; they only move among the floor waiting groups, the in-flight reservations, and the car.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of passengers waiting across all floors, plus those reserved in flight, plus those already in the car, always equals the fixed passenger count present at the start.

EXTENDS Naturals

Ctrls == {g1, g2, g3}
Amt == [c \in Ctrls |-> 1]
Cap == 2
Duration == 2
MaxT == 3

VARIABLES clock, expiry, up, pending
vars == <<clock, expiry, up, pending>>

Live(c) == expiry[c] > clock
LiveAmt(c) == IF Live(c) THEN Amt[c] ELSE 0
LiveLoad == LiveAmt(g1) + LiveAmt(g2) + LiveAmt(g3)

  /\ clock = 0
  /\ expiry = [c \in Ctrls |-> 0]
  /\ up = [c \in Ctrls |-> TRUE]
  /\ pending = [c \in Ctrls |-> FALSE]

Request(c) ==
  /\ up[c] /\ ~pending[c] /\ ~Live(c)
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry, up>>

Grant(c) ==
  /\ up[c] /\ pending[c] /\ ~Live(c)
  /\ LiveLoad + Amt[c] <= Cap
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![c] = clock + Duration]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, up>>

Renew(c) ==
  /\ up[c] /\ Live(c)
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![c] = clock + Duration]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, up, pending>>

ReleaseEarly(c) ==
  /\ Live(c)
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, up, pending>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxT
  /\ clock' = clock + 1

  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry, pending>>

CONSTANTS g1=g1 g2=g2 g3=g3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A power-grid load shedder lets several controllers shed load, but for stability the total load shed at any instant must never exceed a fixed cap. To shed, a controller first raises a request, then must be granted a time-limited lease that authorizes shedding its fixed amount. A lease is granted only if the amount it adds would keep the total currently-leased load within the cap; the lease is stamped with an expiry a fixed duration into the future. A global clock ticks forward, and a lease is considered live only while its expiry is still ahead of the clock, so leases silently lapse as time passes unless renewed. A controller holding a live lease may renew it, pushing the expiry further out, or release it early. Crucially, a controller may crash silently at any time; if it does, it stops renewing and its lease simply expires on its own, freeing capacity without any explicit cleanup. INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shares one critical aisle that spans two segments, each guarded by its own segment arbiter. A robot may drive into the aisle only after a two-phase commit that acquires a grant from every segment arbiter. A robot begins by moving from idle into the voting phase. It then prepares each segment in turn: an arbiter whose segment lock is free grants it to the requesting robot, recording that robot as the lock holder and marking that segment prepared for it. Arbiters may be slow to respond and prepare in any order, but they never fail, so a free segment is always eventually granted. Once a robot has prepared every segment it commits by entering the aisle. When it later exits, it releases all its segment locks and returns to idle. If a robot in the voting phase finds a segment already held by another robot, it cannot gather all grants, so it backs off, releasing whatever locks it did acquire and returning to idle to try again later. A robot is in the aisle only while it holds every segment lock.

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AllAccounted
nl:
A library book-reservation system funnels patron reservation requests through one librarian worker. New requests sit in a backlog and are admitted into a bounded intake queue only while the queue has room; when the queue is full, admission is refused, which is the backpressure that bounds the queue. The librarian processes one request at a time in three steps: it dequeues the head request into its hand and starts reading it, then validates it, then commits it into the shared reservation ledger, after which its hand is empty and ready for the next. The librarian may be slow, taking arbitrarily long between steps and interleaving with new admissions, but it never fails or drops a request mid-way. Consequently every reservation request is always accounted for in exactly one place: still in the backlog, waiting in the intake queue, in the librarian's hand being processed, or recorded in the ledger. No request ever falls out of the system unrecorded.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every reservation request is at all times present in at least one of the backlog, the intake queue, the librarian's hand, or the reservation ledger, so no request's update is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od4m9p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS k1, k2, b1, b2

NONE == "none"
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES epoch, holder, carBay, carEpoch, cstate
vars == <<epoch, holder, carBay, carEpoch, cstate>>

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ holder = [b \in Bays |-> NONE]
  /\ carBay = [c \in Cars |-> NONE]
  /\ carEpoch = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ cstate = [c \in Cars |-> "idle"]

Acquire(c, b) ==
  /\ cstate[c] = "idle"
  /\ holder[b] = NONE
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![b] = c]
  /\ carBay' = [carBay EXCEPT ![c] = b]
  /\ carEpoch' = [carEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
  /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "holding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Release(c) ==
  /\ cstate[c] = "holding"
  /\ carEpoch[c] = epoch
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![carBay[c]] = NONE]
  /\ carBay' = [carBay EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
  /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, carEpoch>>

DropStale(c) ==
  /\ cstate[c] = "holding"
  /\ carEpoch[c] # epoch
  /\ carBay' = [carBay EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
  /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, carEpoch>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ holder' = [b \in Bays |-> NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<carBay, carEpoch, cstate>>

Crash(c) ==
  /\ cstate[c] # "crashed"
  /\ cstate' = [cstate EXCEPT ![c] = "crashed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, carBay, carEpoch>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars, b \in Bays : Acquire(c, b)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Release(c) \/ DropStale(c) \/ Crash(c)
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ Done
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ConsistentHolder ==
  \A c \in Cars, b \in Bays :
    (carBay[c] = b /\ carEpoch[c] = epoch) => holder[b] = c
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS k1=k1 k2=k2 b1=b1 b2=b2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ConsistentHolder
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line assigns cars to wash bays, and periodically reconfigures the line by advancing an epoch counter. Each bay has an authoritative record of its current holder, and each car remembers which bay it grabbed and in which epoch it did so. An idle car acquires a free bay by writing itself into the bay's holder record and stamping its own memory with the current epoch. A car whose stamped epoch still matches the current epoch holds a live claim and may release the bay, clearing the bay's holder record. When the line reconfigures, the epoch advances and every bay's holder record is cleared at once; any car still remembering an older epoch now holds only a stale claim, which it may quietly drop. A car may also crash silently while holding a bay; its stale claim lingers until the next reconfiguration frees the bay. Because a bay's holder record names a single car, and a car counts as holding a bay only when its epoch stamp is current, two cars can never both hold the same bay in the same epoch.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a car's remembered bay claim is stamped with the current epoch, that bay's holder record names exactly that car, so no bay is allocated to two cars in the same epoch.

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker guards a single cross-match station that only one technician may use at a time. Access is arbitrated by one compare-and-swap lock register that is either free or names the technician currently holding it. A technician who wants the station first raises a request, moving from idle to trying. From trying it attempts a compare-and-swap: only if the register reads free does it atomically swap in its own identity, enter the critical section, and become the station's user. While inside, the technician may adjust the shared unit count of the critical blood product up or down within stock bounds; it may take arbitrarily long, being slow, but it never fails or stalls forever. When finished it exits, releasing the register back to free and returning to idle. Because the single register can name only one holder, and a technician is inside only while the register names it, two technicians are never in the station simultaneously, and whenever the register is free nobody is inside.

---- MODULE W4Od11m5p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS s1, s2, s3, u1, u2

Updates == {u1, u2}
Quorums == {Q \in SUBSET Servers : Cardinality(Q) >= 2}

vars == <<stored, committed, proposed, up>>

Init ==
  /\ stored = [s \in Servers |-> {}]
  /\ committed = {}
  /\ proposed = {}
  /\ up = [s \in Servers |-> TRUE]

Propose(u) ==
  /\ u \notin proposed
  /\ proposed' = proposed \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stored, committed, up>>

Ack(s, u) ==
  /\ up[s]
  /\ u \in proposed
  /\ u \notin stored[s]
  /\ stored' = [stored EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {u}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, proposed, up>>

Commit(u) ==
  /\ u \in proposed
  /\ u \notin committed
  /\ \E Q \in Quorums : \A s \in Q : u \in stored[s]
  /\ committed' = committed \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stored, proposed, up>>

Crash(s) ==
  /\ up[s]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stored, committed, proposed>>

Done == (\A s \in Servers : ~up[s]) /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E u \in Updates : Propose(u) \/ Commit(u)
  \/ \E s \in Servers, u \in Updates : Ack(s, u)
  \/ \E s \in Servers : Crash(s)
  \/ Done

    (u \in committed) => \E Q \in Quorums : \A s \in Q : u \in stored[s]

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS s1=s1 s2=s2 s3=s3 u1=u1 u2=u2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CommittedDurable
nl:
A print-shop job spooler replicates its shared job record across three spool servers and commits each update only after a quorum agrees, so that no committed update is ever lost. An update, such as recording a finished print job, is first proposed. Each live server may then acknowledge a proposed update by storing it in its local copy; a server stores any given update at most once and never discards what it has stored. An update becomes committed once there exists some majority quorum of servers all of which have stored it. Because any two majority quorums overlap, a committed update is guaranteed to reside on enough servers that it survives the loss of a minority. A server may crash silently at any time, after which it stops acknowledging new proposals, but the copies it already wrote remain intact on the surviving servers. Thus every update the spooler has committed is durably held by at least one full majority of servers and can always be recovered.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every committed update is stored on all servers of at least one majority quorum, so a committed update is never lost.

---- MODULE W4Od18m3p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS n1, n2, sl1, sl2, o1, o2

  /\ grants = {}

Elect(n) ==
  /\ leader = NONE
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ leader' = n
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED grants

StepDown(n) ==
  /\ leader = n
  /\ leader' = NONE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, grants>>

GrantSlot(n, sl, o) ==
  /\ leader = n
  /\ ~SlotGranted(sl)
  /\ grants' = grants \cup {[slot |-> sl, occ |-> o, term |-> term]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader>>

Release(sl) ==
  /\ SlotGranted(sl)
  /\ grants' = {g \in grants : g.slot # sl}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader>>

Done == (leader = NONE /\ term = MaxTerm) /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n) \/ StepDown(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes, sl \in Slots, o \in Occ : GrantSlot(n, sl, o)
  \/ \E sl \in Slots : Release(sl)

CONSTANTS n1=n1 n2=n2 sl1=sl1 sl2=sl2 o1=o1 o2=o2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT GrantCoherence
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network elects a single leader node that alone is allowed to allocate access slots to occupants. Leadership uses monotonically increasing terms: when there is no leader, any node may stand for election, which installs it as leader and advances the term. The current leader may step down, leaving the network temporarily leaderless until a new election, which is how the network fails over if a leader becomes unresponsive. Only the node that is currently the leader may grant a slot, and it grants a slot to an occupant only if that slot is not already granted to anyone; each grant is stamped with the term in which it was made. A granted slot may later be released, freeing it for future allocation. A leader may be slow but never truly fails, so allocation simply pauses during a leaderless gap and resumes once a new leader is elected. Because there is at most one leader at any moment and the leader refuses to grant an already-granted slot, no access slot is ever handed to two different occupants.
SAFETY PROPERTY: any two recorded grants for the same access slot name the same occupant, so no slot is ever allocated to two different occupants.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m0p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS dr1, dr2, se1, se2
Drones == {dr1, dr2}
Sectors == {se1, se2}
NONE == "none"
MaxVer == 3

VARIABLES owner, sver, snap, dstate, target
vars == <<owner, sver, snap, dstate, target>>

Init ==
  /\ owner = [s \in Sectors |-> NONE]
  /\ sver = [s \in Sectors |-> 0]
  /\ snap = [d \in Drones |-> [s \in Sectors |-> 0]]
  /\ dstate = [d \in Drones |-> "idle"]
  /\ target = [d \in Drones |-> NONE]

Read(d, s) ==
  /\ dstate[d] = "idle"
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![d][s] = sver[s]]
  /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![d] = s]
  /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "reading"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, sver>>

Claim(d) ==
  /\ dstate[d] = "reading"
  /\ LET s == target[d] IN
       /\ owner[s] = NONE
       /\ sver[s] = snap[d][s]
       /\ sver[s] < MaxVer
       /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = d]
       /\ sver' = [sver EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "holding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, target>>

Retry(d) ==
  /\ dstate[d] = "reading"
  /\ LET s == target[d] IN
       owner[s] # NONE \/ sver[s] # snap[d][s] \/ sver[s] >= MaxVer
  /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, sver, snap, target>>

Release(d) ==
  /\ dstate[d] = "holding"
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![target[d]] = NONE]
  /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sver, snap, target>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Drones, s \in Sectors : Read(d, s)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Claim(d) \/ Retry(d) \/ Release(d)

HeldConsistent ==
  \A d \in Drones : dstate[d] = "holding" => owner[target[d]] = d
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS dr1=dr1 dr2=dr2 se1=se1 se2=se2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT HeldConsistent
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm partitions the burn area into sectors, and each drone tries to claim a sector to monitor, using optimistic locking with retry. Every sector has an owner field, empty or a drone, and a version counter that increments whenever the sector is successfully claimed. To claim, an idle drone first reads a target sector, snapshotting that sector's current version. It then attempts the claim, which succeeds only if the sector is still unowned and its version still equals the snapshot the drone took, meaning no other drone claimed it in between; on success the drone becomes the owner, the version advances, and the drone is holding. If instead the sector is now owned or its version has moved, the optimistic attempt failed, so the drone backs off to idle and may retry later. A holding drone may release its sector, clearing the owner. Drones may be slow, interleaving their reads and claims arbitrarily, but none fails outright. The version check is exactly what stops a slow drone from claiming a sector that another drone grabbed after it read.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a drone is in the holding state for its target sector, that sector's owner field names that same drone, so no sector is ever held by two drones at once.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS r1, r2, r3
Reqs == {r1, r2, r3}
Cap == 2

VARIABLES backlog, ready, buffer, serviced, opens
vars == <<backlog, ready, buffer, serviced, opens>>

Init ==
  /\ backlog = Reqs
  /\ ready = {}
  /\ buffer = {}
  /\ serviced = {}
  /\ opens = 0

Enqueue(r) ==
  /\ r \in backlog
  /\ backlog' = backlog \ {r}
  /\ ready' = ready \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<buffer, serviced, opens>>

Admit(r) ==
  /\ r \in ready
  /\ Cardinality(buffer) < Cap
  /\ ready' = ready \ {r}
  /\ buffer' = buffer \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, serviced, opens>>

Cancel(r) ==
  /\ r \in ready
  /\ ready' = ready \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, buffer, serviced, opens>>

Service(r) ==
  /\ r \in buffer
  /\ r \notin serviced
  /\ buffer' = buffer \ {r}
  /\ serviced' = serviced \cup {r}
  /\ opens' = opens + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, ready>>

Done == backlog = {} /\ ready = {} /\ buffer = {} /\ UNCHANGED vars

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS r1=r1 r2=r2 r3=r3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnceLatched
nl:
An elevator bank services hall-call requests, where actually dispatching a car to a floor is an irreversible physical action that must happen at most once per request. Requests arrive into a backlog, are enqueued into a ready set, and from there are admitted into a bounded dispatch buffer, but only while the buffer has room; when it is full, admission is refused, providing backpressure. Because the network delivers and reorders freely, both admission from the ready set and selection from the buffer pick an arbitrary request rather than following any fixed order. To service a request the dispatcher takes it from the buffer, provided it has not already been serviced, performs the one-time car dispatch (incrementing the total dispatch count), and records the request as serviced. A ready request may instead be cancelled and dropped before ever being buffered. Once a request has been serviced it is removed from every holding area, so it can never re-enter the pipeline and never be dispatched a second time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: any request that has been serviced is absent from the backlog, the ready set, and the dispatch buffer, so no request can ever be dispatched more than once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m3p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS a1, a2, b1, b2, c1, c2, p1, p2, iA, iB
Instances == {iA, iB}

Authority to operate the pool is granted as a time-limited lease carrying a fencing token. Granting a lease to a controller that has no live lease first bumps the pool's authoritative token to a fresh, strictly higher value, then hands that new token to the controller and sets its lease to expire a fixed duration ahead on the global clock. nl:
Two independent settlement engines share one pool: a single shared record listing which interbank updates have been applied, guarded by a version counter for optimistic concurrency. To apply an update, an engine first reads the shared record, snapshotting both the current set of applied updates and the current version, and noting which update it intends to add. It then commits only if the version has not changed since its snapshot, meaning no other engine wrote in between: it writes back its snapshot extended with its update and bumps the version, and records that update in its own private log of successful commits. If the version has moved, its optimistic attempt is stale, so it retries by discarding its snapshot and reading afresh. An engine may also voluntarily abandon a pending attempt. Because a commit is accepted only when the snapshot version still matches, no engine ever overwrites another engine's contribution with a stale snapshot. Consequently every update an engine has recorded as committed remains present in the shared applied record.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every update that an engine has recorded in its private log of successful commits is still present in the shared applied record, so no committed update is ever lost.

nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser has one controlled-substance dispensing station that only a single pharmacist may operate at a time. Access is fenced by an epoch counter. An idle pharmacist acquires the station only when it is free, recording itself as the station holder and stamping its own memory with the current epoch as it starts dispensing. It finishes dispensing only while its stamped epoch still matches the current epoch, which frees the station. A pharmacist may crash silently while dispensing; it then stops on its own but its stale hold on the station lingers. To recover, the pharmacy reconfigures: it advances the epoch and force-clears the station, which fences out any crashed or stale holder because that holder's stamped epoch no longer matches the current epoch. A non-crashed pharmacist that notices its stamp is stale simply drops back to idle. Because the station record names a single holder and a pharmacist counts as validly dispensing only while its epoch stamp is current, no two pharmacists ever validly operate the station in the same epoch.
SAFETY PROPERTY: any pharmacist that is dispensing with an epoch stamp equal to the current epoch is exactly the pharmacist named in the station record, so at most one pharmacist validly operates the station at once.

---- MODULE W4Od17m8p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS ro1, ro2, ch1, ch2
Routers == {ro1, ro2}
Chutes == {ch1, ch2}
NONE == "none"
TOTAL == 2

VARIABLES bags, transit, coarse, fine, rphase, rdst
vars == <<bags, transit, coarse, fine, rphase, rdst>>

Init ==
  /\ bags = [c \in Chutes |-> 1]
  /\ transit = [r \in Routers |-> 0]
  /\ coarse = NONE
  /\ fine = [c \in Chutes |-> NONE]
  /\ rphase = [r \in Routers |-> "idle"]
  /\ rdst = [r \in Routers |-> NONE]

GrabCoarse(r) ==
  /\ rphase[r] = "idle"
  /\ coarse = NONE
  /\ coarse' = r
  /\ rphase' = [rphase EXCEPT ![r] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bags, transit, fine, rdst>>

GrabFine(r, c) ==
  /\ rphase[r] = "coarse"
  /\ fine[c] = NONE
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![c] = r]
  /\ rdst' = [rdst EXCEPT ![r] = c]
  /\ rphase' = [rphase EXCEPT ![r] = "fine"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bags, transit, coarse>>

PickUp(r, src) ==
  /\ rphase[r] = "fine"
  /\ bags[src] >= 1
  /\ bags' = [bags EXCEPT ![src] = @ - 1]
  /\ transit' = [transit EXCEPT ![r] = 1]
  /\ rphase' = [rphase EXCEPT ![r] = "carrying"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, rdst>>

Drop(r) ==
  /\ rphase[r] = "carrying"
  /\ bags' = [bags EXCEPT ![rdst[r]] = @ + transit[r]]
  /\ transit' = [transit EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![rdst[r]] = NONE]
  /\ coarse' = NONE
  /\ rphase' = [rphase EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
  /\ rdst' = [rdst EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]

Abort(r) ==
  /\ rphase[r] \in {"coarse", "fine"}
  /\ coarse' = NONE
  /\ fine' = [c \in Chutes |-> IF fine[c] = r THEN NONE ELSE fine[c]]
  /\ rphase' = [rphase EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
  /\ rdst' = [rdst EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bags, transit>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Routers : GrabCoarse(r) \/ Drop(r) \/ Abort(r)
  \/ \E r \in Routers, c \in Chutes : GrabFine(r, c)
  \/ \E r \in Routers, src \in Chutes : PickUp(r, src)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BagsConserved ==
  (bags[ch1] + bags[ch2]) + (transit[ro1] + transit[ro2]) = TOTAL
====

nl:
An airport baggage router moves bags between chutes using two-level hierarchical locking to stay conflict-free. To perform a move a router must first acquire the single coarse region lock, and only then a fine lock on a specific destination chute; the coarse-before-fine order is mandatory. Once holding both locks a router picks up one bag from some source chute, carrying it in hand, and then drops it into its locked destination chute, after which it releases both the fine and the coarse locks and returns to idle. A router that has taken locks but not yet picked up a bag may instead abort, releasing whatever locks it holds. Because routing messages arrive over the network in any order, routers choose their destination and source chutes arbitrarily and interleave their steps freely. Throughout all of this, bags are only ever moved from a chute into a router's hand and then into another chute; none is ever created or lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of bags sitting in all chutes plus the number currently being carried in transit by routers always equals the fixed total number of bags present at the start.
